Frequently Asked Questions

Reach Out Today

  • How does epoxy flooring hold up in Ohio winters?

    Epoxy flooring systems built with proper surface preparation handle Ohio's freeze-thaw cycles, road salt, and moisture exceptionally well. The seamless coating prevents salt and water from penetrating the concrete. At Apex Epoxy Flooring Solutions, we use premium coatings designed specifically for Northeast Ohio's climate conditions.

  • What's the difference between metallic and flake epoxy flooring?

    Metallic epoxy creates flowing, high-end visual effects ideal for showrooms and modern spaces, while flake epoxy provides textured, slip-resistant surfaces suited for garages and commercial areas. Both offer durability, but flake systems handle heavy traffic and provide more traction. The choice depends on your aesthetic goals and functional needs.

  • Why is concrete surface preparation important for epoxy?

    Mechanical grinding removes contaminants, weak surface layers, and old coatings to ensure proper adhesion between epoxy and concrete. Without it, coatings can peel or fail prematurely. At Apex Epoxy Flooring Solutions, we use precision mechanical prep on every project to maximize long-term durability and performance.

  • Can epoxy flooring be applied to basement concrete?

    Yes, epoxy flooring works well on basement concrete when the slab is properly prepared and moisture levels are acceptable. It creates a moisture-resistant, easy-to-clean surface that resists staining. A professional inspection helps determine if the slab condition is suitable for coating installation.

  • How long does an epoxy floor coating last?

    With proper surface preparation and quality materials, epoxy floor coatings typically last 10 to 20 years in residential garages and 5 to 15 years in high-traffic commercial settings. Longevity depends on traffic levels, maintenance, and climate exposure. Precision prep and premium coatings maximize lifespan in Ohio's demanding conditions.

  • What affects the cost of commercial epoxy flooring?

    Cost depends on square footage, surface condition, coating type, and prep requirements such as grinding or repairs. High-traffic industrial floors require thicker systems than light commercial spaces. At Apex Epoxy Flooring Solutions, we provide free inspections and estimates to assess each facility's needs accurately.

  • Is flake epoxy flooring slip resistant?

    Yes, flake epoxy flooring provides a textured, slip-resistant surface ideal for garages, commercial spaces, and areas exposed to moisture or vehicle traffic. The decorative flakes are broadcast into the coating, then sealed with a clear topcoat. This system balances safety, durability, and visual appeal.

  • When should you seal concrete instead of coating it?

    Concrete sealing is best when you want basic protection from moisture and staining without changing the surface appearance or adding a thick coating. It's often used on driveways, patios, and warehouse floors. Epoxy coatings provide more durability and design options for high-use interior spaces.

  • What's the biggest mistake people make with garage epoxy?

    Skipping proper surface preparation is the most common mistake, leading to poor adhesion and premature coating failure. DIY kits often lack the mechanical grinding needed to open concrete pores. At Apex Epoxy Flooring Solutions, we use precision grinding to ensure every coating bonds correctly and lasts for years.

  • How do you maintain a polished concrete floor?

    Polished concrete requires regular dust mopping and damp cleaning with a pH-neutral cleaner to preserve the finish. Avoid harsh chemicals or abrasive scrubbing. Periodic repolishing can restore gloss over time. The low-maintenance surface resists staining and wear, making it ideal for commercial and residential interiors.

  • Can epoxy flooring be installed over existing coatings?

    Only if the existing coating is fully bonded and in excellent condition, which is rare. Most old coatings must be mechanically removed to ensure proper adhesion. At Apex Epoxy Flooring Solutions, we inspect and grind surfaces to remove failing layers and create a clean, profiled substrate for lasting results.

  • What are the benefits of metallic epoxy in showrooms?

    Metallic epoxy creates unique, flowing visual effects that elevate modern showrooms, retail spaces, and high-end interiors. The seamless, reflective finish is easy to clean and highly durable. At Apex Epoxy Flooring Solutions, we customize each metallic system to match design goals while ensuring long-term performance.

  • How long before I can drive on epoxy?

    Most residential epoxy installations take 1 to 2 days to complete. Light foot traffic is typically safe after 24 hours, but waiting 5 to 7 days before parking vehicles ensures the system is fully cured. Fast-curing polyaspartic topcoats can shorten that return-to-service time significantly.

  • Can epoxy coatings fix cracked or damaged concrete?

    Epoxy coatings protect and seal — they aren't structural leveling compounds. However, minor cracks, pitted areas, and spalling are repaired with high-strength concrete patch materials during mechanical surface preparation before coating begins, ensuring a smooth, seamless finished surface.

  • Are epoxy floors slippery when wet?

    Smooth epoxy can become slippery when exposed to water, snow melt, or oil. Slip-resistant aggregates or anti-slip additives — such as decorative flakes or quartz granules — are incorporated into the topcoat to ensure safe traction, especially in garages and commercial spaces exposed to Ohio winters.

  • What gloss levels does polished concrete come in?

    Polished concrete ranges from a low-sheen matte to a mirror-like high gloss depending on the number of diamond grinding passes and the hardness of the slab. A satin finish suits residential basements, while retail and commercial spaces often choose a reflective, high-gloss result.

  • Does moisture in the slab affect epoxy installation?

    Yes — high moisture vapor can cause epoxy to bubble, delaminate, or fail at the bond line. A moisture test is performed during the inspection phase. When vapor levels are too high, a vapor barrier primer is applied first, or the project is delayed until slab conditions are within acceptable range.

  • Why choose professional epoxy over a DIY kit?

    DIY store kits typically use thin, water-based formulas that lack the bond strength of professional-grade systems. Without mechanical diamond grinding to open the concrete pores, adhesion fails quickly. Professional installation uses industrial equipment, proper primers, and thicker coating systems built to last years under real-world traffic.

  • Can epoxy floors include safety zone color coding?

    Yes. Commercial and industrial epoxy systems can incorporate color-coded lanes, hazard zones, or pedestrian pathways directly into the coating design. This is common in warehouses, manufacturing facilities, and government buildings where OSHA visual safety standards require clear floor markings.

  • How often should epoxy floors be professionally cleaned?

    An annual professional cleaning helps maintain coating performance and appearance, especially in garages and commercial spaces exposed to road salt and grime. Professional scrubbing and pressure washing removes buildup that routine mopping leaves behind, preserving the topcoat and extending the floor's overall lifespan.

  • Is epoxy flooring a good fit for retail spaces?

    Retail floors benefit from epoxy's combination of seamless appearance, stain resistance, and easy cleaning between customer visits. Decorative flake and polished concrete options create stylish surfaces that handle foot traffic, rolling carts, and regular cleaning cycles without fading, cracking, or requiring specialty maintenance products.

  • What makes epoxy a smart choice for property managers?

    Epoxy and concrete coatings protect parking garages, mechanical rooms, lobbies, and storage areas against moisture, salt, and surface breakdown. The sealed surface reduces long-term maintenance costs and improves appearance across multi-unit and commercial portfolios — making it a practical, cost-effective investment for Northeast Ohio properties.
